terminology.details: byte is now defined and related to generation positions. TOOL is the request action, calculator its allowed name, and 1+2 the ordered inputs; allowlist explicitly means permitted tool names. The trace is hand-written, raw holds its text, and eos=True is a manually supplied ending claim, not a model-generation trace. EOS is an ending ID rather than a correctness guarantee. DIRECT and ASK are supplied by 19.1. action_trace is first generated output, runtime the actual execution, and final_trace the generated readback answer. action_correct requires the full first string and EOS; end-to-end correctness also checks final content. joint is the joint text/image/audio training version and DPO is identified as a later preference-trained branch. No undefined term prevents me from explaining the section.

own_explanation.problem_and_flow: The runtime only solves the request it receives. A mistaken request solves a different question; a correct request can still be followed by a wrong model answer. Record and compare the original question, first model request/EOS, runtime result, and second model response/EOS.
own_explanation.inputs_and_symbols: raw is the request string; eos is the artificial ending flag in the local example. parse_action returns a structured action; a and b hold the ordered integer addends. available is the True/False runtime switch. A successful result is a string in a dictionary. The plus sign means ordinary addition.
own_explanation.numbers: SFT reports 10/10 for each complete-calculation gate, 10/10 unavailable cases, and 5/5 independent readback questions. Final joint reports 12/12 correct requests and executions but 10/12 correct final answers, with 12/12 unavailable cases and 5/6 independent readback. The held-out 1+2 and 2+1 both reach generated answer 3. Distinct denominators cannot be added into one loop count.
